::: {#sol-shift-all}

`(lambda (x) (* x x))` is the function that squares its argument,
written in place without a name.

1. Applying it to 7 returns 49.
2. `map` (@exm-map-filter) applies the doubling function to each element, and returns `'(2 4 6)`.
3. In the body of `shift-all`, `d` is 10,
   so `map` applies the function $x \mapsto x + 10$ to each element, and returns `'(13 11 14)`.

:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
#### Source

`shift-all` is adapted from Jerry Cain's `translate` in his CS 107 handout "Scheme: Functions As Data" [@cain2008cs107],
used under the [Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 United States License](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/us/).
It is renamed, translated from Scheme to Racket, and recast as an exercise with new inputs.
:::
